paper_type_rationale: ASPIRE introduces a new robotic agentic coding framework with three novel components (closed-loop execution engine, skill library, evolutionary search). This is a methods/system paper: the contribution is the architecture itself, validated by quantitative experiments on multiple benchmarks.
must_cover: Three-component architecture (execution engine / skill library / evolutionary search)
Multimodal trace mechanism for failure attribution
Skill library as accumulated cross-task knowledge
Quantitative results on LIBERO-Pro / Robosuite / BEHAVIOR-1K / LIBERO-Pro Long
Zero-shot generalization on unseen long-horizon tasks
Comparison to prior coding agents (CaP-Agent0, OpenVLA, pi0, pi0.5)
key_numbers: +77% success rate improvement on LIBERO-Pro perturbation
150+ sim tasks used to build the skill library
N=90 skill library size for zero-shot transfer
Library size N=0 -> 90 monotone scaling in zero-shot success
real_comparisons: ASPIRE vs CaP-Agent0 (Fu et al. 2026): prior code-as-policy baseline across all benchmarks
ASPIRE vs OpenVLA / pi0 / pi0.5 (VLA model baselines) on LIBERO suite
ASPIRE vs pi0-s (zero-shot variant) on LIBERO
With-skills vs without-skills (ablation on real-robot tokens and success rate)
Library size N=0/25/50/90 scaling (ablation on accumulated experience)

central_claims.claim: Closed-loop multimodal trace execution engines dramatically improve failure localization compared to coarse rollout-level feedback
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Per-primitive trace inspection enables targeted repairs validated by +77% gain on LIBERO-Pro perturbation
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: That traces alone suffice — ASPIRE combines traces with skill library and evolutionary search

central_claims.claim: A continually growing skill library transfers validated fixes across tasks, simulation, and embodiments
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Library N=0 -> 90 monotonically improves zero-shot success; 31% vs 4% on LIBERO-Pro Long zero-shot
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: Full library transfer to a new embodiment — only 3 skills validated on real bimanual robot

central_claims.claim: Evolutionary search over diverse program candidates explores beyond single-trajectory refinement
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: +32% on BEHAVIOR-1K long-horizon procedural layouts where single-trajectory debugging plateaus
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: Compute cost advantage — no wall-clock vs accuracy tradeoff reported

central_claims.claim: The combination of execution engine + skill library + evolutionary search yields +32-77% gains on short-horizon manipulation and 7-8x zero-shot on long-horizon tasks
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Combined system beats strongest baselines (CaP-Agent0, OpenVLA, pi0) on every benchmark evaluated
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: Generalization to entirely new task domains without library seeding

claim_boundaries: Real-robot transfer evidence is limited to three simulation-discovered skills on a single bimanual embodiment
Comparison set on LIBERO includes strong but dated VLA baselines (OpenVLA, pi0); newer VLAs (pi0.5, GR00T N1) absent
Skill library quality depends on accumulated experience — bootstrapping on a new domain starts cold
Evolutionary search is compute-intensive; no wall-clock vs accuracy tradeoff reported
negative_or_limiting_results: OpenVLA and pi0 achieve 0% success on LIBERO object/goal/spatial positional tasks — strong negative baseline
Skill transfer on real robot only validated for 3 specific skills, not full skill library
No comparison against recent pi0.5 / GR00T-N1 / Helix on LIBERO-Pro

mechanism_result_map.result: Enables per-primitive failure attribution -> enables targeted repairs -> validates the +77% gain on LIBERO-Pro perturbation tasks
Distills validated fixes as transferable knowledge -> grows monotonically with N -> yields 31% zero-shot LIBERO-Pro Long success vs 4% baseline
Samples diverse candidate programs -> explores beyond single-trajectory refinement -> validates +32% on BEHAVIOR-1K long-horizon

comparative_positioning: Differs from CaP-Agent0 (Fu et al. 2026) by adding per-primitive multimodal traces (vs coarse rollout feedback) and a persistent cross-task skill library (vs per-task fixes)
Differs from prior code-as-policy (HiP, ProgPrompt) by accumulating experience into reusable skills rather than re-prompting per task
Aligns with agentic coding trend (Anthropic / OpenAI / SWE-bench agents) by applying software-engineering-style iterative debugging to robotics
Complementary to VLA models (pi0, pi0.5, OpenVLA) — VLA provides manipulation primitives; ASPIRE composes them via code
reuse_takeaways: Pattern: closed-loop execution with multimodal traces > naive rollout feedback for any agentic robot code-generation system
Pattern: explicit skill library as a first-class persistent artifact across sessions and embodiments
Pattern: evolutionary search over diverse program candidates complements single-trajectory self-improvement
Anti-pattern: per-task fixes discarded at task completion — kills cumulative learning
Anti-pattern: relying on coarse task-level success/fail signal alone for failure diagnosis
followup_questions: How does skill library quality scale with simulator diversity (Isaac Sim only vs multiple physics backends)?
What is the compute cost of evolutionary search per task vs baseline agent debugging time?
Does skill transfer generalize across different robot embodiments (Franka vs ALOHA vs Unitree)?
Can the skill library be pre-seeded from human demonstrations rather than autonomous exploration?
How does ASPIRE compare against pi0.5 / GR00T-N1 / Helix on the same LIBERO-Pro benchmarks?

section_plan.focus: Title, authors, affiliations, venue, arXiv id, date — 12 fixed metadata fields in canonical order.
Faithful Chinese translation of the abstract, preserving the three-component claim and all key numerical gains (+77%, +72%, +32%, 31% vs 4%).

4-6 numbered innovations: (1) closed-loop multimodal trace engine, (2) persistent cross-task skill library, (3) evolutionary search over programs, (4) coordinator-actor parallel learning, (5) sim-to-real cross-embodiment skill transfer.
One paragraph synthesis: ASPIRE = closed-loop execution + skill library + evolutionary search, yielding +32-77% on short-horizon and 7-8x zero-shot on long-horizon manipulation tasks.

Two sub-problems: (a) naive execution environments provide only pass/fail, hindering failure diagnosis; (b) existing systems discard experience across tasks, so the hundredth task is no easier than the first.

Benchmarks: LIBERO-Pro (perturbation), Robosuite (contact-rich bimanual), BEHAVIOR-1K (long-horizon household with procedural layouts), LIBERO-Pro Long (zero-shot unseen). Hardware: Franka + bimanual setup. Simulation: Isaac Sim + LIFE.

Three components: (1) closed-loop execution engine exposes per-primitive multimodal traces; (2) skill library distills validated fixes as reusable cross-task knowledge; (3) evolutionary search samples diverse program candidates and conditions next generation on survivors.

+77% on LIBERO-Pro perturbation; +72% on Robosuite bimanual handover; +32% on BEHAVIOR-1K; 31% vs 4% zero-shot on LIBERO-Pro Long; library size N=0 -> 90 monotone scaling; real-robot tokens reduction with skills.

Why multimodal traces work (per-primitive attribution vs coarse feedback); why skill library transfers across tasks and embodiments; where evolutionary search adds value; what ASPIRE does NOT solve (compute cost, cold-start, comparison to newer VLAs).
Limited real-robot evidence (3 skills, 1 embodiment); dated VLA comparison set; no compute cost analysis; no library seeding from human demonstrations.

Reusable patterns (closed-loop traces, persistent skill library, evolutionary search); replication suggestions (start with execution engine + small library); followup reading (CaP-Agent0, agentless, Anthropic SWE-bench).
Primary citation (Lu et al. 2026); key related work (Anthropic 2025, OpenAI 2025, Fu et al. 2026 CaP-Agent0, OpenVLA, pi0/pi0.5, LIBERO benchmarks).
